newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends higher on soybean rally, funds buy.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends higher on soybean rally, funds buy.

text.p: CBOT corn futures ended higher on Thursday, boosted by gains in soybeans and fund buying that totaled at least 30 million bushels, traders said.
News South Africa's corn crop was expected to be well below last year's output was also supportive.
South Africa's National Crop Estimates Committee said on Thursday it estimated the 1997 maize crop at 7.564 million tonnes, down sharply from last year's 9.484 million tonnes.
Traders also noted USDA put corn net export sales during the week ended March 13 at 867,700 tonnes, near the high end of expectations for 650,000 to one million tonnes.

Gains were trimmed late on local selling. Traders also said the market had underestimated the significance of an outbreak of foot and mouth disease in Taiwan that forced a ban on Taiwanese pork exports.
"I think people are underestimating the Taiwan thing," a trader said. "It's a bigger deal than they thought."
Floor sources cited reports from Taiwan that corn imports would fall by 20 percent, or roughly 120 million tonnes of feed corn per year.
Corn ended 3-1/4 to 1-1/2 cents per bushel higher with May up 1-1/2 at $3.04-3/4.
On the day, Cargill Inc bought five million bushels July and three million December but sold six million May. FCC bought two million July and sold one million December.
Griffin Trading bought 12 million bushels, divided between the May and July, and Refco Inc bought six million May and five million July. Smith Barney bought five million July.
Continental Grain spread 12 million July/May and six million December/May while Prudential Securities spread four million May/July.
In options trade, ING sold 1,000 May $3.00 calls at 13 cents. Prudential Securities bought 400 May $3.00 calls and 400 May $3.00 puts at 20 to 20-1/2 cents.
Corn volume was estimated by CBOT at 80,000 contracts, compared with Wednesday's actual volume of 50,920.
